fields.title: Osteoarthritis
fields.bodyHtml:
Osteoarthritis: advanced treatment in Israel

Osteoarthritis is the most common form of arthritis, marked by the gradual thinning of the cartilage in the joints, which leads to pain, stiffness and reduced movement. Israel offers innovative approaches to its treatment, combining international experience, highly qualified specialists and the latest advances in medical science.

Diagnosis of osteoarthritis

  1. Clinical examination
    The doctor assesses the patient's symptoms and medical history and carries out a physical examination to identify painful joints and those with restricted movement.
  2. X-rays
    Allow the extent of joint damage to be assessed, along with the presence of erosion and bony outgrowths (osteophytes).
  3. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    Used for a more detailed assessment of the cartilage, the joint capsule and the surrounding soft tissue.
  4. Laboratory tests
    Blood tests may be ordered to rule out other forms of arthritis, such as rheumatoid arthritis.

Methods of treating osteoarthritis in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Drug therapy
      The use of NSAIDs, chondroprotective agents and corticosteroid injections to reduce pain and inflammation.
    • Physiotherapy
      Individual exercise programmes to strengthen the muscles and improve joint movement.
    • Orthopaedic aids
      The use of braces, orthoses and specialist footwear to reduce the load on the affected joints.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Intra-articular injections of hyaluronic acid
      Improve lubrication of the joint and its mobility.
    • Arthroscopy
      Minimally invasive surgery to remove damaged cartilage and osteophytes.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Joint replacement
      Replacement of the affected joint with an artificial implant, recommended in severe osteoarthritis.
    • Osteotomy
      Surgical realignment of the limb to redistribute the load on the joint.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Advanced medical technology
    The use of the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment.
  • Experienced specialists
    Leading orthopaedic surgeons and rehabilitation specialists of international standing.
  • An individual approach
    Every patient is offered treatment adapted as closely as possible to their needs and way of life.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Integrated rehabilitation programmes help achieve the best possible recovery of joint function after treatment.

Treatment of osteoarthritis in Israel gives patients the chance of considerable relief from symptoms, an improved quality of life and a return to an active life.

fields.title: Astrocytoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Astrocytoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Astrocytoma is a type of glioma — a tumour arising from the glial cells of the brain. These tumours vary in how malignant they are, from slow-growing to highly aggressive forms. In Israel, patients with astrocytoma are offered a comprehensive approach to diagnosis and treatment based on the latest research and innovative technologies.

Diagnosis of astrocytoma

  1. MRI of the brain
    The main diagnostic method, establishing the position, size and structure of the tumour.
  2. CT of the brain
    May be used for additional imaging of the tumour and assessment of its effect on the surrounding structures.
  3. Biopsy
    Carried out to obtain a sample of tumour tissue, which is examined to determine the type of tumour and how malignant it is.
  4. Laboratory tests
    Include blood tests to assess general health and identify possible markers of inflammation or other changes linked to the tumour.
  5. Genetic testing
    May be recommended to identify specific mutations in the tumour cells, which can affect the choice of treatment.

Treatment of astrocytoma

  1. Surgery
    The primary and often most effective treatment, aimed at removing as much of the tumour as possible.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used after surgery to destroy remaining tumour cells, particularly in high-grade astrocytomas.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used in combination with other treatments to fight the tumour, particularly in aggressive forms of astrocytoma.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest approaches to treating astrocytoma, directed at specific molecular targets and at stimulating the immune system to fight the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment
    Access to the newest technologies and treatments, including minimally invasive surgery and personalised therapy.
  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Specialists from various fields of medicine work together to develop the best treatment plan for each patient.
  • Individual treatment
    Treatment programmes are adapted to each patient, taking account of every aspect of their health and the specific nature of the tumour.
  • Comprehensive support
    Psychological, social and rehabilitation support is provided at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of astrocytoma in Israel combines high medical expertise, access to innovative technologies and a deep understanding of patients' needs, which produces the most effective results and improves patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Atherosclerosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Atherosclerosis: advanced treatment in Israel

Atherosclerosis is a chronic condition marked by the formation of plaques in the arteries, which impairs the blood supply to the organs and tissues. In Israel, innovative approaches are used to treat atherosclerosis, aimed at slowing the progression of the disease and preventing complications.

Diagnosis of atherosclerosis:

  1. Laboratory tests
    Full blood count, cholesterol tests, lipid profile, markers of inflammation and other biochemical markers.
  2. Ultrasound examination of the vessels (Doppler)
    Assessment of the state of the arteries and of any atherosclerotic changes.
  3. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Imaging of the arteries to identify narrowed sections and assess the plaques.
  4. Angiography
    An invasive investigation that establishes precisely how far the vessels are narrowed.

Methods of treating atherosclerosis:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Statins and other lipid-lowering drugs to control cholesterol levels.
    • Antihypertensive drugs to control blood pressure.
    • Drugs that prevent blood clots, such as aspirin or other antiplatelet agents.
  2. Surgical treatment:
    • Angioplasty with stenting: widening the narrowed sections of the vessels and fitting a stent to keep them open.
    • Coronary artery bypass grafting: creating bypass routes for the blood around the narrowed sections of the coronary arteries.
    • Endarterectomy: surgical removal of atherosclerotic plaques from the arteries.
  3. Changes in lifestyle:
    • A balanced diet: low in saturated fat and cholesterol and rich in fruit, vegetables and whole grains.
    • Regular physical exercise: helps improve circulation and reduce weight.
    • Giving up smoking: smoking considerably increases the risk that atherosclerosis will progress.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: cardiologists, vascular surgeons and dietitians work together to create the best treatment strategy.
  • Personalised treatment: an individual treatment programme is chosen on the basis of thorough diagnosis and the particular condition of each patient.
  • Access to advanced technology: the use of the newest medical technologies and techniques in treating atherosclerosis.
  • A high standard of medical care: experienced specialists and medical staff providing high-quality treatment and support at every stage of treatment and recovery.
  • Treatment of atherosclerosis in Israel is aimed at actively improving the condition of the vessels, reducing the risk of cardiovascular complications and providing long-term prevention to maintain patients' health and quality of life.

fields.title: Optic nerve atrophy
fields.bodyHtml:
Optic nerve atrophy is a condition in which the nerve fibres of the optic nerve degenerate, leading to progressive loss of sight. The causes may include inherited disease, inflammation, injury, poisoning and other factors.

Diagnosis of optic nerve atrophy

The following methods are used in Israel to diagnose optic nerve atrophy accurately:

  1. Detailed review of the medical history: the doctor talks with the patient about their medical history, including symptoms, the events preceding the illness, previous conditions and treatment.
  2. Visual examination: the doctor examines the patient's eyes, looking for possible changes in the structure of the fundus, the diameter of the pupil and other signs of optic nerve atrophy.
  3. Measurement of vision: visual acuity is tested both with Snellen charts and with specialised optical instruments.
  4. Visual field testing: special tests such as perimetry may be used to assess the function of the optic nerve and establish whether the patient has any restriction of the visual field.
  5. Optical coherence tomography (OCT): a scan of the eye that produces high-quality images of the structures of the fundus, including the optic nerve and retina.
  6. Retinal angiography: where necessary, retinal angiography may be carried out to assess the blood supply to the eye and identify any conditions associated with optic nerve atrophy.
  7. Consultation with a neuro-optometrist or neuro-ophthalmologist: the patient discusses the results of all the investigations with a specialist, who provides the diagnosis and advice on further treatment and management.
  8. Explanation and treatment planning: on the basis of the diagnostic results the doctor explains to the patient the nature of the condition, its possible causes and the best treatment options. An individual management plan is drawn up, which may include drug treatment, rehabilitation or surgery.

Methods of treating optic nerve atrophy

Advanced methods of treating optic nerve atrophy are used in Israel:

  1. Drug therapy: includes medicines that improve the blood supply and metabolic processes in the optic nerve.
  2. Vitamin therapy: the use of B vitamins, antioxidants and neuroprotective agents to support the health of the nerve cells.
  3. Physiotherapy: methods such as magnetic therapy, ultrasound therapy and electrical stimulation help stimulate the regeneration of nerve fibres.
  4. Laser therapy: used to improve the blood supply and nutrition of the nerve tissue.
  5. Electrical stimulation: helps activate the remaining healthy nerve fibres.
  6. Surgical treatment: in rare cases this may be needed to remove the cause of the atrophy (decompression of the optic nerve, for example).

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli doctors have rich experience and international recognition in ophthalmology.
  2. Modern equipment: clinics are equipped with the newest diagnostic and treatment instruments, which ensures accuracy and effectiveness.
  3. An individual approach: every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of all aspects of their health.
  4. Interdisciplinary collaboration: doctors of various specialities work closely together to achieve the best treatment results.
  5. High standards of safety and quality: Israeli clinics adhere strictly to international protocols and standards of medical care.

Treatment of optic nerve atrophy in Israel gives patients access to highly qualified medical care, improves their quality of life and helps preserve their sight for many years.
